meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law with Islamic Sharia influence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Arab Republic of Egypt and the United States of America for the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (effective 1992)
Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments between Egypt and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (effective 1975)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, as amended by Laws No. 78 of 2003, No. 181 of 2008, No. 36 of 2014, and No. 72 of 2017, together with its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 3121 of 2002; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the beneficial ownership register schedule established by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Executive Regulations; Law No. 106 of 2013 on Small, Micro and Medium Enterprises as amended; Law No. 84 of 2002 on Private Associations and Private Foundations as applied to the charitable-purpose endorsement; Central Bank of Egypt Regulation No. 1050 of 2020 on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each natural-person founder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the founder's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction, followed by authentication by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies or commercial registry in the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; consular stamp is mandatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian limited liability company and appointing its local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign corporate shareholder's board of directors and local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds documentation for the initial capital transfer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing jurisdiction; consular legalization required when the bank reference is incorporated into a notarially executed bundle

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Arabic-language memorandum of association and articles of association for the Egyptian LLC (GAFI standard form)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary bureau recognized by the Egyptian Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization followed by deposit with GAFI; no apostille required for an internal Egyptian document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each founder, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner against the Egyptian AML Unit's domestic PEP register, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (including resolution 1267/1989), the US OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Egyptian domestic terrorism designations issued by the Ministry of Justice. Exact-match hits are escalated to the designated compliance officer. PEPs, their family members, and close associates are subject to enhanced customer due diligence under Law No. 80 of 2002 and applicable GAFI and Central Bank of Egypt guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Company Name Reservation and Commercial Registry portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg/) operated together with the Commercial Registry Offices of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; private charitable endowment activity also requires a name authorization comment from the Ministry of Social Solidarity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Arabic script, followed by the entity type modifier 'ذات مسئولية محدودة' (limited liability company). An English transliteration may appear only in parentheses as a secondary commercial reference and must preserve the exact Arabic name order. Latin-script prefixes, numerals, and academic or governmental titles are not permitted in the corporate name except with ministerial approval.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Central Bank, Insurance, Securities, Deposit, Savings, Finance, Investment Fund
Ministry, Presidential, Military, Police, National Guard, National Intelligence
Charity, Donation, Philanthropic, Zakat, Awqaf (requires prior approval of the Ministry of Social Solidarity)
International, Arab Republic, United States, Union, Co-operative
Misr, Al-Ahram, Al-Amal when used as a distinctive state-affiliated expression
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, GAFI issues a written notice identifying the statutory ground. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 business days, presenting the original reservation receipt and an alternative name. The Committee must render a decision within 30 days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file an annulment action before the Economic Court within 60 days of the decision notice; no additional fee is charged for the original applicant when the appeal proposes an identical-name or transliteration correction.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. A virtual or serviced office is accepted as a registered address for the GAFI incorporation of a limited liability company. However, because the business scope includes ISIC 6430 endowment management for a private charitable foundation, the Ministry of Social Solidarity requires evidence of a physical office presence through a lease or serviced-office contract demonstrating continuous local management. A pure virtual address without an authorized local manager will not satisfy the charitable-purpose licensing review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium, quantified at approximately 45% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operation, reflecting Egypt's risk-based supervision of licensed non-profit endowment-management entities and the AML/CFT inspection priorities of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance reservation and commercial registry search (one primary and one alternative company name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the GAFI fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and bilingual (Arabic/English) notarization of the articles of association and memorandum of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed notarial fee schedule plus translation certification; prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of foreign corporate shareholder documents (passports, certificates, board resolutions) and Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Embassies or Consulates and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT beneficial ownership screening and PEP/sanctions background verification for each founder and UBO covering UN, OFAC, EU, and Egypt AML lists
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI-authorized compliance firm and the Egyptian AML & CFT Unit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark at USD 200 per screened natural person, averaged at four persons

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Charitable-purpose pre-licensing endorsement and legal-pattern review by the Ministry of Social Solidarity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for non-profit activity endorsement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI registration fee for incorporation of the limited liability company under Company Law No. 159 of 1981
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and GAFI fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation summary in the Egyptian Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Misriya) and in a Cairo or Alexandria daily newspaper
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official Gazette Board and licensed Egyptian daily newspaper

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / serviced address arrangement for the first 12 months of the foundation management office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed serviced-office provider in New Cairo or Alexandria
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for serviced address plus local business license

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2013 (Limited Liability Company provisions, Articles 102-135); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (GAFI registration and guarantees); Registrar of Foundations provisions under Law No. 84 of 2002 for grant-making endorsement; Egyptian Civil Code endowment rules for philanthropic capital
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop Shop for Investor Services, Cairo; Commercial Registry under Ministry of Interior, Cairo Governorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Eshar Ta'sis) executed before a GAFI-certified notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 159/1981; however, the Ministry of Social Solidarity charitable license requires an initial endowment of EGP 250,000 (approx. USD 5,150) evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued by an Egyptian licensed bank
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers unanimously adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company and accept the allotment of shares as set forth therein, the subscribed share capital being fully paid into the Company's bank account. RESOLVED further that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [address], Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt, and the authorized officer be instructed to execute the lease in favour of the Company. RESOLVED further that Mr. [name] be appointed Chairman and Managing Director, and Mr. [name] be appointed Corporate Secretary, with joint authority to open bank accounts, execute statutory filings, engage auditors, and apply for all licenses required for charitable endowment and grant-making operations, including registration with GAFI, the Tax Authority, and the Ministry of Social Solidarity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Economic Substance Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop — online investor portal 'Invest in Egypt' (www.investinegypt.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application via the GAFI e-portal selecting 'Limited Liability Company' and 'charitable foundations / endowment activities'. The name shall include the format '[Name] for Philanthropic Endowments LLC'. Trigger automated screening against the Trade Register and Ministry of Social Solidarity restricted-name list. Upon approval, the name reservation is valid for 90 days; download the official certificate.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all subscribers (minimum one subscriber, non-resident ownership permitted)
Board resolution of each corporate subscriber approving the investment in Egypt
Power of attorney for the Egyptian founder representative, notarized and legalized
Feasibility statement and proposed endowment activity description
Certificate of good standing for any foreign corporate subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or meaning, submit two alternative names within 3 working days; if a legal merit issue is raised, apply for the GAFI Pre-Application Ruling under Investment Law Article 24 within 15 days, or request a meeting with the GAFI Appeals Unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarized Execution and Authentication of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Legal Department / Notary Public Office attached to the One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic (with an English translation annexed for the non-resident shareholders), stating the capital, shares, purpose, board powers, establishment of the endowment fund, and liquidation rules. All subscribers or their attorneys-at-law appear before the notary; pay stamp duty (0.4% of authorized capital) and notarial fees. The notary endorses the founding charter and forwards it for GAFI registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (Arabic)
Name reservation certificate from Step 1
Proof of subscribers' identities and legal capacity
Endowment bank deposit certificate in a licensed Egyptian bank
Consent of the registered-office landlord with certified copy of the title deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a substantive defect (unlawful purpose, share allocation issue, or defective capital clause), rectify and re-pay only the incremental stamp duty; a certified correction may be made by supplementary resolution without full re-execution unless Articles have already been published.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing and Issuance of Commercial Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop — Commercial Registration Department (in coordination with the Cairo Commercial Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized founding charter with the Commercial Registry through the One-Stop Shop. The registry examines the business form, purpose, and the compatibility with ISIC 6430/NAICS 813211. Upon approval, issue the Commercial Registration (CR) certificate containing the entity's registry number, paid-up capital, and permitted objects. The CR certificate must be collected in person or by the authorized attorney.
required_dossiers: Notarized and authenticated Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI incorporation application form
Proof of payment of GAFI fees and publication contribution
Registered office lease agreement and building occupancy permit
Board resolution on incorporation and management appointments
Letter from the bank confirming the capital-funded escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries mismatches between the stated purpose and ISIC code, submit an explanatory memorandum and amended Articles approved by the shareholders; if the objection is based on pending investigations, await the GAFI legal opinion, which must be rendered within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Gazette and Deposit of Capital Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Publication Unit / Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya (Official Gazette) and licensed Egyptian bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company publishes an incorporated-entity notice in the Official Gazette within 30 days of CR registration, stating the entity's name, registry number, capital, and registered office. Simultaneously, maintain the paid-up capital in an escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank and obtain the bank's capital deposit certificate of EGP 250,000 for the charitable endowment as required by the Ministry of Social Solidarity licensing conditions.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Publication request form signed by the Managing Director
Bank capital deposit certificate (EGP 250,000)
Specimen signature card of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is delayed beyond 30 days, pay the late fine and submit a notarized affidavit explaining the delay; the GAFI publication unit may expedite within 2 working days if the delay is caused by bank processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Tax EIN, VAT and Withholding Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Investment Branch, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Integrated Tax Registration Form using the CR certificate to obtain the Tax Card and Tax Identification Number (EIN). Register for VAT, withholding tax, and payroll tax. For a charitable foundation, apply for the tax exemption status of investment returns, which requires a separate application to the ETA Exemptions Section under Income Tax Law 91/2005 Article 26; obtain the exemption certificate before the first grant distribution.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office lease contract
Board resolution appointing the tax representative and accounting firm
Bank account certificate and capital deposit confirmation
Bank endorsement letter for the charitable expenditure program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA queries the charitable purpose or the exemption application, submit the Ministry of Social Solidarity preliminary approval letter and the endowment deed; if a tax audit is triggered, engage an Egyptian licensed tax advisor and respond within the 15-day statutory reply period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance Registration and Employment Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) — Cairo Integrated Service Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company and its founding employees with NOSI within 30 days of CR registration. File the Form 1 registration under Social Insurance Law 148 of 2019 and Form 2 for each employee. The foundation must adopt an internal employment, safety, and grant-management policy to satisfy the Ministry of Social Solidarity inspection standards.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Tax Card (EIN and VAT certificate)
Founding employment contracts of all managers and staff
Identification documents and social insurance form of employees
Board resolution adopting the social insurance declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI issues an arrears assessment, submit proof of timely payment and payroll records; file an administrative objection with the NOSI Dispute Committee within 30 days if the assessment is erroneous; late registration fines may be waived upon a formal written justification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Social Solidarity — Civil Society Organizations and Foundations Development Authority, in coordination with GAFI One-Stop Shop
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: License to Practice Charitable Endowment Management and Grant Distribution (Tarkhees Idarat Al-Waqf Al-Khairi)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — pursuant to Environmental Law 4 of 1994 as amended by Law 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Low Impact — Registration / No Full EIA Report); office-based endowment management generates no industrial emissions and requires only a self-declaration and registration with the EEAA regional branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law 48/1982 and EEAA Decree 92/2013: domestic wastewater (sewage) may be discharged solely into the public sanitary sewer; solid waste (paper, e-waste) classified as municipal waste under Decree 92/2013 and must be collected by an EEAA-licensed contractor; negligible VOC or particulate emissions for office activity; air quality within premises per the workplace standard of Decree 209/2005; no hazardous chemical storage thresholds triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Pre-occupancy Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Civil Defense Administration (Ministry of Interior) after inspection of fire extinguishers, marked exits, and smoke detectors; structural load inspection report of the registered office by a licensed structural engineer confirming safe occupancy; Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) workplace clearance under Labor Law 12 of 2003 and Ministerial Decree 211/2003, including first-aid kit, emergency lighting, and employee safety training records; the license holder must apply for annual renewal and submit to the Central Inspection of the Ministry of Social Solidarity for grant-disbursement transparency review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), operating under the Ministry of Finance. Official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg. Mandatory electronic invoicing and e-receipt clearance portal: https://www.invoice.eta.gov.eg. The ETA administers the Integrated Tax Code comprising income tax (Law 91/2005), VAT (Law 67/2016), stamp duty, and the Unified Tax Procedures Law (Law 25/2020). For private charitable foundations, the Ministry of Social Solidarity co-grants the founding licence under Law 149/2019 on Non-Governmental Organizations and Private Foundations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned LLC establishing in Egypt must: (1) notarize the memorandum and articles of association and register with the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry; (2) obtain the charitable foundation licence from the Ministry of Social Solidarity under Law 149/2019 where the LLC operates as a private charitable endowment vehicle; (3) file the unified tax registration application with the ETA, attaching certified constitutional documents, board resolution appointing a resident tax representative, registered address evidence, passport copies of shareholders/managers, and legalized incorporation documents of any non-resident corporate founder; (4) upon verification, receive the unified 9-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) covering income tax, VAT, stamp duty, and the e-invoicing profile. Separate VAT registration is required once annual taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000 (or voluntarily from EGP 250,000). Non-resident suppliers without an Egyptian establishment are not eligible for VAT registration and instead trigger the Egyptian resident recipient's reverse-charge obligation. The TIN is a precondition for bank account opening, customs clearance, and issuance of fiscally valid e-invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed on worldwide taxable income at the standard corporate income tax rate of 22.5% for tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2023. LLC earnings are subject to entity-level CIT; distributions are not deductible. A licensed private charitable foundation is eligible for a limited-purpose income tax exemption under Article 114 of Law 91/2005 where the ETA confirms that the endowment income is applied exclusively to philanthropic, scientific, or public-benefit grant-making purposes. Unrelated commercial or investment income not deployed for the approved charitable objects remains taxable at the entity level. Egypt does not recognize pass-through taxation for LLCs; the classification is fixed by commercial legal form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not offer US-style check-the-box or hybrid pass-through elections; entity classification is determined by legal form. Available statutory mechanisms include: (1) VAT group registration for related Egyptian persons under Article 16 of Law 67/2016, allowing consolidated VAT filing and netting of input/output VAT before the ETA upon prior approval; (2) voluntary VAT registration for persons with annual taxable supplies between EGP 250,000 and EGP 500,000; (3) Advance Pricing Agreements with the ETA for cross-border related-party arrangements; (4) annual application for charitable income tax exemption under Article 114 of Law 91/2005, subject to ETA listing, audited accounts, and renewal; (5) voluntary self-correction/disclosure procedures with reduced penalties under Law 25/2020. Hybrid mismatch anti-abuse is addressed through general anti-abuse rules, Egyptian CFC provisions, thin-capitalization limits, and beneficial-ownership/economic-substance audit practice rather than formal elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value Added Tax under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, supplemented by the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 25 of 2020. Egypt does not apply GST or sales-and-use tax; VAT is levied on taxable supplies of goods and services in the territory and on imports of goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration applies to any person whose taxable supplies of goods and services exceed EGP 500,000 over any rolling 12-month period. Voluntary registration is permitted for taxable supplies above EGP 250,000 per annum. Exempt non-profit activities are excluded from taxable turnover for threshold measurement. Non-resident suppliers with no Egyptian fixed establishment have no registration threshold and the Egyptian recipient must self-assess VAT via the reverse-charge mechanism on imported services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance applies to all VAT-registered businesses. Taxpayers must transmit electronic invoices (B2B) and electronic receipts (B2C) to the ETA through the official portal or certified ERP integration in JSON format. Each invoice is digitally signed with an ETA-issued e-certificate (SHA-256 digest and RSA signature) and receives a unique UUID and submission code from the ETA before it acquires fiscal validity. Rejected invoices are invalid for input VAT recovery and expose the issuer to penalties. Rollout phases for e-invoicing and e-receipts are fully operative; the ETA enforces compliance by suspending TIN credentials and e-invoicing profiles for non-compliant registrants.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 23 of VAT Law 67/2016, exports of goods and services are zero-rated. Goods qualify when they physically depart Egyptian customs territory under a valid customs export declaration, are sold to a non-resident buyer, and are shipped within the statutory export period. Services qualify when supplied to a non-resident recipient with no Egyptian establishment and the service is consumed wholly outside Egypt. International transport and directly related services are also zero-rated. For a private charitable foundation, pure grant disbursements and endowment donations are outside the VAT charge as non-economic transfers; however, management fees invoiced to offshore endowment funds and scientific grant-administration services supplied to non-residents consumed abroad may qualify for 0% VAT provided the foreign recipient-beneficiary test, foreign-currency invoicing, and offshore-use substantiation are met. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable and produces refundable positions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (certified customs release proving physical departure of goods from Egypt, matching commodity code, quantity, and value)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (or multimodal transport document naming a consignee outside Egypt and confirming shipment out of Egyptian territory)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorized Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in convertible foreign currency within the prescribed repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may re-open export zero-rating claims and refund positions for the statutory assessment period despite completed refunds. Fraudulent or fictitious zero-rated exports, including sham transport documents, false foreign-currency invoicing, or non-repatriation of proceeds, trigger retrospective clawback of the VAT refund and related input credits, plus late-payment additional tax at 2% per month or fraction thereof. Administrative penalties per invoice, criminal fines, imprisonment for wilful tax evasion, strike-off from the exporter priority-refund registry, suspension of the TIN, and joint liability of foundation principals and responsible officers may be imposed. Documentary integrity, matching of the customs export declaration with the e-invoice submission, and CBE-compliant foreign-currency repatriation are the primary audit focal points.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – Foreign Exchange Operations Sector and Banking Supervision Sector
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates an overall managed float; current account transactions are largely liberalized, while capital account operations remain subject to CBE registration and approval. Profit remittance to non-resident investors is permitted through the receiving licensed bank, contingent on CBE registration of the original inward capital injection, audited financial statements, local tax clearance, and compliance with Law 194/2020. For a private charitable foundation, 'profit' is limited to income derived from managing its endowment; donor grants are not distributable as profit, and any conversion or onward remittance of foreign-currency grants is subject to enhanced source-of-funds and purpose-of-gift reviews.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt within 90 days from the date of bill of lading or due shipment date unless a CBE-approved extension is obtained. Under the current liberalized regime, no mandatory conversion ratio is imposed; exporters may retain foreign currency in a CBE-approved export proceeds account. The foundation itself, being an endowment-management entity with no export trade, remains subject to the same statutory framework if it undertakes any incidental export activity. Failure to repatriate within the 90-day window exposes the entity to penalties under the CBE Banking and Credit Law No. 194 of 2020 and associated sanctions regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, etc.) do not possess a CBE license and cannot serve as principal treasury rails for an Egyptian-domiciled LLC/foundation. CBE regulations require all corporate FX and cross-border settlement to be executed through banks licensed under Law 194/2020. Such EMIs may only be used as ancillary collection/payment tools where they ultimately route funds through a CBE-supervised bank, but the foundation must maintain its primary operational and escrow accounts at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank for statutory and compliance reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBE KYC rules require physical appearance of all authorized signatories, at least one director, and each ultimate beneficial owner at a branch of the selected Egyptian bank for identity verification and the corporate KYC interview. Remote opening is generally not permitted for initial onboarding of an entity with non-resident ownership or charitable status. Exceptions apply only to supplementary signatory additions or ongoing account maintenance. The foundation must present original corporate documents, certified Arabic translations, and original identity records for each person attending.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Charitable/pass-through fund classification and non-commercial purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original certificate of incorporation under the Egyptian NGO/foundation framework (Law 149/2019), not-for-profit articles of association, registered endowment deed, board resolution on grant-making policy, audited financial statements proving non-commercial activity, and a detailed AML/governance manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore donor concentration or large initial endowment injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth declaration for each major donor, donor KYC pack (passport, proof of address and source of funds), prior financial institution reference for the donor, CBE source-of-funds form, and legal opinion on the donor's legitimacy and compliance with Egyptian currency controls.

Exhaustive beneficiary registry, grant award agreements, beneficiary KYC/GIS screening, distribution approval minutes, legal basis for each transfer, and a CBE no-objection letter or continued-online declaration for each outward remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEP) or sanctioned-jurisdiction nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contemporaneous PEP and sanctions screening snapshots, board-approved PEP declarations, compliance officer sign-off, transaction-specific justification, and a final legal opinion confirming compliance with CBE, UN, and EU sanctions frameworks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections (endowment transfers, grants, donations) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to a CBE-licensed bank account in the foundation's name. The remitter must include a purpose code corresponding to 'transfers for social/charitable services' or 'capital endowment injection' as defined in CBE transaction classification guidelines. The foundation must file the mandatory foreign-funding declaration with the Ministry of Social Solidarity under Law 149/2019, and obtain a CBE no-objection confirmation for any intended conversion to EGP. All inbound funds must be matched to the foundation's CR (commercial registry) extract and Egyptian tax card; no third-party pass-through is permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements, whether grant distributions or payments for cross-border goods/services, are executed via SWIFT MT103 in the designated settlement currency through the foundation's CBE-supervised bank. For cross-border import of goods eligible under the foundation's activities, irrevocable commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) or documentary collections are available from tier-1 Egyptian banks with a valid foreign trade underlying approval. The bank requires pro forma invoices, grant approval minutes, a CBE FX transaction advice, and, where relevant, the reserve bank notification for outward transfers above the CBE reporting threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards with underlying trade or grant-settlement exposure, undertaken through a CBE-authorized bank

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) when the underlying exposure is documented and the transaction is executed through a CBE-authorized onshore bank or a licensed offshore correspondent under CBE-permitted trading
Cross-Currency Swaps for asset/liability alignment on major endowment inflows and outflows, subject to CBE counterparty authorization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form No. 1 for legal persons) with audited financial statements and tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end no later than 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 2% per month of unpaid tax, capped at 100% of assessed tax, plus late-payment interest; persistent non-filing is treated as tax-evasion evidence and may lead to criminal referral and asset attachment before administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GAFI annual accounts deposit: certified financial statements, shareholders' approval minutes, and the manager's annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, Ministry of Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of the accounting year-end; must be uploaded to the GAFI investor portal before the shareholders' meeting is filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning after 60 days' delay; non-deposit blocks commercial-registry services; continued failure for one full year allows GAFI to commence compulsory strike-off and liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership and statutory register confirmation via the GAFI electronic annual questionnaire
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit for AML/CFT data exchanges
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year companies must complete the confirmation before 31 March; shareholding transfers and UBO changes must be reported within 15 days of each transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or incomplete UBO confirmation subjects the managers to the penalties of Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002, including fines up to EGP 100,000 and imprisonment for deliberate concealment, independent of company strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration renewal, annual fee settlement, and activity-license annual validation for the charitable endowment management license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry; co-confirmed by GAFI for the licensed activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Commercial-registration certificates are renewable every five years, but the annual registry tariff and license validation must be paid no later than 31 January of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a surcharge equal to 10% of the annual fee, with an additional 10% per further year of delay; an unrenewed and inactive company for two consecutive years is referred by GAFI to the competent court for compulsory strike-off and liquidation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Egyptian Companies Law No. 159/1981 as amended by Law No. 4/2016, an LLC must appoint an independent certified auditor when: (i) the Articles of Association or shareholders' agreement mandates audit; (ii) the company's paid-up capital exceeds EGP 250,000; (iii) annual turnover exceeds EGP 5,000,000; (iv) the number of shareholders exceeds ten; or (v) a regulatory authority — in this case the charitable-endowment licensing authority — requires audit as a license condition. A private charitable foundation managing endowment assets is always subject to statutory audit because it administers third-party beneficiary funds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), as issued by Ministry of Investment Decree No. 110/2018 and aligned with IFRS for fair-presentation companies; tax-prepared financial statements follow the Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91/2005.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain at its registered office a full register of members, managers, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners. The Annual GAFI compliance confirmation restates the natural persons holding at least 25% of capital, voting rights, or control. Every share-transfer event, including transfers to a charitable beneficiary or endowment trustee, must be recorded in the members' register and notified to GAFI within 15 days. The annual confirmation is due with the GAFI accounts deposit and must be certified by the manager; no separate UBO fee is assessed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assembly and Management Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300–700 USD per year for a registered office and corporate agent in Cairo or a GAFI-governed branch office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500–4,000 USD per year for a small-to-mid-size Egyptian LLC with foundation activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory zero-rate for registered private charitable foundations under Article 51(3) of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, provided endowment returns are applied exclusively to philanthropic and scientific grants, the foundation is licensed under NGO Law No. 149/2019, and no non-qualifying commercial activity is conducted. Non-exempt business profits are taxed at 22.5%; donors benefit from statutory deduction ceilings for qualified contributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 41 filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified e-filing portal (Misr Digital / tax.gov.eg) by the LLC's licensed public accountant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year (Article 36, Law No. 91/2005); a calendar-year foundation must file no later than 30 April of the following year. Quarterly self-assessed advance instalments apply during the year under Articles 27-29.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and gains including endowment investment returns, interest, rentals and grant-related receipts applied to the charitable objects.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing entity is the resident Egyptian LLC; non-resident beneficiaries are not taxpayers on this return. Foreign-sourced endowment income is reported gross with foreign tax evidence attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Article 51 exempt resources: subsidies, grants, donations, zakat and charitable endowment proceeds legally confined to the foundation's stated purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only amounts covered by the NGO registration, audited allocation statements and donor restriction letters; attach the license decision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses directly incurred in generating taxable revenues; dual-use and administrative overheads are apportioned on an audited basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border fees such as consultants, cloud services and IP licences must be evidenced by contracts and satisfy the withholding tax and transfer pricing regime; otherwise they are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss of any commercial or promotional segment unrelated to the charitable objects; this forms the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign grant funds applied to the non-exempt segment are taxable; reclassify and support the allocation with a functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses claimed against current taxable profit, limited to five years from the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a non-resident without a permanent establishment cannot be surrendered into the Egyptian return; the LLC's own losses require audited annual filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 4 minus Box 5, after transfer pricing adjustments and statutory disallowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify DTA-induced adjustments, thin capitalisation limits and withholding tax gross-ups before netting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable corporate rate of 22.5% applied to Box 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foundation remains liable at 22.5% on non-qualifying profits; no treaty rate applies to the LLC's own Egyptian tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax produced on the non-exempt segment after allowed credits and investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show the Article 51 exempt share in a reconciliation schedule; the ETA audited allocation of exempt assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly self-assessed instalments, bank interest withholding credits and foreign tax credits reducing the liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bank interest WHT certificates and foreign TRC-backed credits must be retained in the LLC's tax file; uncredited amounts trigger objections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax payable or claimable refund after all advances, with payment instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder has no entitlement to refunds due to the LLC; subsequent distributions are subject to the 10% dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: statutory fine of no less than EGP 20,000 and no more than EGP 100,000 on the legal person (Article 137); monthly delay surcharge of 1.5% of the unpaid corporate tax (Article 33); the ETA may raise additional assessments for five years and refer intentional omissions for criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on profit distributions to non-resident shareholders without an Egyptian permanent establishment (Article 56, Law No. 91/2005); resident Egyptian corporate shareholders may rely on inter-corporate dividend relief subject to participation requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), beneficial ownership declaration and, where the treaty requires, a certificate evidencing the 10% or 25% shareholding to the Egyptian LLC before payment. The LLC retains the documents, applies the reduced DTA rate in the e-tax portal and annexes the treaty relief claim to its Form 41 annual file; over-withheld amounts are recovered through a refund claim or the Mutual Agreement Procedure under the applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and licence fees for IP use: 20% domestic WHT; interest on cross-border loans: 20% domestic WHT. Bilateral DTAs typically reduce these rates to 10-15% for royalties and interest; higher rates apply where the recipient is a bare nominee rather than the beneficial owner. Payments lacking economic substance or failing limitation-on-benefits clauses are recharacterised as hidden profit distributions and lose treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million aggregate controlled transactions per fiscal year triggers the Local File; the Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated revenues exceed EGP 1.5 billion (ETA Transfer Pricing Decisions Nos. 457-458 of 2020).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Article 51 exemption, Article 30 GAAR and substance-over-form practice impose equivalent conditions: the foundation must hold genuine board meetings in Egypt, maintain a local grant pipeline, employ substantive staff, keep segregated charitable bank accounts and document each financing arrangement. A letter-box charitable vehicle loses the exemption and attracts back taxes and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting endowment investment income, inflating grant-distribution costs, issuing fictitious expense vouchers, maintaining two sets of books, or destroying records to understate Form 41 taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Articles 133-136 of Law No. 91/2005 as amended: imprisonment generally up to five years, fines scaled to the evaded tax, compulsory civil restitution, 1.5% monthly delay surcharge and revocation of the charitable license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil in fraud and sham structures; directors and signatories are jointly and severally liable for the foundation's tax debt, face travel bans and asset freezes by ETA collection units, management disqualification and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell charitable entity / sham economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registration as a private charitable foundation solely to route foreign donations or endowment funds to offshore co-venturers without genuine Egyptian charitable activity, using nominee directors and lacking operational premises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA retroactively revokes the Article 51 exemption, taxes accumulated endowment returns at 22.5%, imposes delay surcharges and fines, and invokes Article 30 GAAR to recharacterise the structure; license cancellation under Law No. 149/2019 may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners are identified through anti-avoidance disclosure; directors are jointly liable for restored tax, named in criminal referrals and subject to travel bans while the liability remains unpaid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / counter-terrorist financing and NGO licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting anonymous cash endowments, distributing cash grants without client due diligence, transacting with sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, or making undisclosed cross-border fund transfers inconsistent with the declared grant purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002 and counter-terrorism Law No. 94/2015: fines up to EGP 10,000,000, confiscation and freezing orders, imprisonment up to 15 years for responsible directors, and blacklisting of the foundation by the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors bear individual criminal liability for wilful blindness in grant disbursements, are subject to travel bans and deportation measures, and face personal asset freezing where foundation funds were used to conceal illicit proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax and DTA abuse on repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, royalties, interest or service fees to non-residents without the statutory 10% or 20% withholding, or applying treaty rates on forged TRCs, backdated share certificates or nominee recipients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The LLC remains liable as debtor for the un-withheld tax (Article 59) plus the 1.5% monthly delay surcharge and a fine up to EGP 100,000; false TRC usage triggers criminal fraud charges, restitution and recapture of treaty benefits with interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign withholding declarations are personally liable for uncollected amounts, face civil prosecution for misapplication of company funds, and may be banned from cross-border travel until tax clearance is issued.
